title: Private deployment activation & customer enablement playbook for RBAC / Audit / KMS
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Objective: deliver an operationalized launch and customer activation plan for Private/VPC/on-prem features (RBAC, audit logging, KMS integration) that meets enterprise compliance requirements and enables SRE/Platform customers to self-activate in a controlled manner.

Scope:
- Release notes and staged communications for Early Access (EA) customers -> Staged GA -> Broad availability.
- Runbook and security-ops checklist for customers and Redwood field engineers.
- Customer enablement content: onboarding checklist, quickstart scripts, guided upgrade notes, and a pre-flight validator.
- Cross-team GTM tasks: Sales + Solutions collateral, Support playbook, Professional Services enablement, and release notes coordination with Developer Docs and SDK teams.

Decisions made so far:
- Choose phased rollout (EA -> limited GA -> broad GA) to limit blast radius for RBAC/KMS keying. EA customers will get manual provisioning via Solutions Eng; limited GA will enable self-serve activation in console with guardrails.
- Audit log retention defaults: 90 days in-hosted console views; customers can configure exports to customer-managed sinks (S3/BigQuery). This balances storage cost with compliance needs.
- KMS integration will support two modes initially: customer-managed AWS KMS keys (recommended) and Redwood-managed keys for low-risk customers. Full HSM-backed HSM path deferred to post-GA.

Key deliverables:
- Release notes draft (developer docs and user-facing) with clear breaking-change notice for on-prem upgrade flows.
- Security & compliance runbook (internal) for incident response and data-subject requests.
- Customer-facing onboarding guide and pre-flight validator script.
- Training session materials for Sales, Support, and Solutions Engineering (slides + recorded session).
- Telemetry dashboard in Console showing RBAC policy application rate, audit-log ingestion health, KMS key usage, and errors.

Rollout plan (high level):
1) 2026-02-10: Internal enablement week (trainings, runbook dry-run, support drills).
2) 2026-02-17: Early Access invites go out; 5 selected customers onboarded with Solutions Eng assistance.
3) 2026-02-24: Validate telemetry and runbook; iterate on pre-flight tool.
4) 2026-03-01: Limited GA (customers who opt in via console); release notes published and customer comms sent.
5) 2026-03-15: Broad GA pending post-GA health check and Exec sign-off.

Communication cadence:
- Weekly PM sync (Wed 10am PT) to track blockers and coordinate docs/PRs.
- Slack channel: #pm-private-deployments for async updates.
- PRD/FAQ canonical location on Confluence; do not duplicate in Drive.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Self-serve vs assisted onboarding: self-serve reduces manual load but increases upfront risk; decided to gate self-serve behind a pre-flight validator for limited GA.
- Retention and export defaults: default 90 days reduces cost for Redwood-hosted preview but requires robust export docs.
- KMS breadth at GA: supporting fewer KMS providers reduces QA surface; we will support AWS KMS first, with GCP KMS and Azure Key Vault in the following quarter.
